title: Hoi An still keeps the 14th for lanterns
summary: The ancient town still marks the 14th night of each lunar month with candles and lanterns. The July 2025 notice does not print a clock or a ticket. The hour, and the next civil date, are check on arrival.
when: The 14th night of each lunar month. The hour is check on arrival.
photoAlt: Lanterns on the river in Hoi An at night
body: Hoi An’s lantern night is still tied to the lunar calendar, not to a fixed Gregorian evening. The conservation centre’s notice of 8 July 2025 says the ancient town gives up electric light on every 14th night, and that local groups keep music, poetry, chess, bài chòi, tuồng, and folk singing. That notice names the contact square at Quảng trường Sông Hoài. It does not print a start time, and it does not sell a ticket for the night.

One civil date is already in the past. The 2026 Nguyên tiêu plan put that cycle’s lantern night on 2 March. The same pages do not list the next 14th. Go by the lunar night, and check the hour and the civil date on arrival.

sources.label: Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre, 8 July 2025
